mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.15%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.15% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 235.0, it signals accelerating inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 235.0 (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 3-month moving averages signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between PAYEMS and HOUST both rising and SPX 60-day returns is negative (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, strong housing market activity (HOUST > 1200.0) reflects sustained consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST > 1200.0 (t-test p > 0.05 vs. positive return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0) indicates weakening economic output, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 105.0 (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE ≤ 5.0%) reflects a tight labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE ≤ 5.0% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. positive return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: The combination of low FEDFUNDS (≤ 0.15%) and rising CPIAUCSL (≥ 235.0) signals imminent monetary tightening due to inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.15% and CPIAUCSL ≥ 235.0 yields positive SPX 20-day returns in > 60% of instances (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST > 1200.0) indicate strong consumer demand for residential construction, supporting economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST > 1200.0 (t-test p > 0.05 vs. positive return expectation).
